**Step-by-step reasoning:**

1.  **Calculate the current inventory of water bottles:**
    Bill has 2 cases of water, and each case contains 24 bottles.
    $$ 2 \text{ cases} \times 24 \text{ bottles/case} = 48 \text{ bottles} $$

2.  **Calculate the total number of bottles required:**
    Bill has 70 guests and wants to provide 2 bottles of water for each guest.
    $$ 70 \text{ guests} \times 2 \text{ bottles/guest} = 140 \text{ bottles} $$

3.  **Calculate the additional bottles needed:**
    Subtract the number of bottles Bill already has from the total number of bottles required to find out how many more he needs to buy.
    $$ 140 \text{ total bottles needed} - 48 \text{ bottles already owned} = 92 \text{ additional bottles} $$

The calculations are consistent across all peer responses and my previous analysis.

Final answer: 92
